source_location.original_identifier: Reader III, editorial lines5–6: gé mē drincan ne sealdon

supports.text: For give someone to drink, use sęllan with the person in the dative and plain drincan, without tō. Apply the already known singular command and pronoun forms. This entire construction is supplied for this item.
supports.change_note: The exact source has a negative past statement; the English Cook item asks for a positive singular command. This help transfers only the bounded person-plus-infinitive frame, not an unrestricted purpose construction.

source_location.original_identifier: Reader III, editorial lines12–14 and original note17

supports.text: Use the supplied connection swā lange swā for the opening As long as. Cook’s note17 explains the biblical expression as inasmuch as: the deeds done to the hungry are counted as done to the Lord. Both swā words belong to this whole connection; the earlier so/thus sense does not teach it. The two you references are plural; use the taught past forms and case frames.
supports.change_note: Only the connecting expression and its sense are transferred from the named source passage. The assigned English item changes the subordinate action to feeding the hungry; no general temporal-clause system is independently tested.
